subject: Business Models
title: Master Franchise Agreements
description: A quick win: understand Master Franchise Agreements.

hook.text: Want to bring Starbucks to South Korea? Buy a master franchise license for the entire country.

buildup.text: Master franchisees buy the right to sub-franchise an entire region. They become the local franchisor.

discovery.text: This lets the brand expand without understanding local regulations, culture, or real estate markets.

twist.text: Master franchise fees for major markets can exceed $10 million. It's a bet on an entire country's appetite.

climax.text: Master franchising is how most US brands went global. Local partners handle what headquarters cannot.

punchline.text: Buy one country's rights, sub-franchise every city. That's the master deal.

quiz.question: What does a master franchisee do?
options: Buys regional rights and sub-franchises to others

details.summary: A master franchise agreement grants an entity the right to sub-franchise an entire region or country. The master franchisee essentially becomes the franchisor within their territory, recruiting and supporting individual franchisees while paying the parent company a portion of all fees collected.
details.whyItMatters: Master franchising is how brands like McDonald's, KFC, and Subway expand internationally without the parent company managing operations in every country..
takeaways: Master franchisees become sub-franchisors within their defined territory
They recruit, train, and support individual franchisees in the region
This model enables rapid international expansion using local market expertise

faq.question: How does a master franchise arrangement differ from a regular franchise?
faq.answer: A regular franchisee operates one or more locations directly. A master franchisee operates as a mini-franchisor within a territory, selling and managing individual franchise agreements. They earn a portion of every franchisee's fees rather than just operating their own units.

faq.question: What are the risks of master franchise agreements?
faq.answer: Master franchisees must invest heavily upfront for territory rights, often millions of dollars. They bear responsibility for an entire market's development timeline. If they fail to recruit sufficient sub-franchisees or maintain quality standards, they risk losing the master agreement.
